The country has been under martial law since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022, meaning elections have been suspended. "Democracy cannot be held hostage by Russia," said Fedorov, 35, in a video posted to YouTube on Tuesday, adding that Ukraine is fighting "precisely because we want to remain a free European state". Since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022 Ukraine has been under martial law, which means elections are suspended. Fedorov, who did not mention Zelensky by name in the video, was unexpectedly fired from his role as defence minister in late July, just six months after his appointment. stories.title: How to grow food for more people in a hotter world
stories.summary: Inside futuristic labs, plants are scanned, stressed and analyzed. The aim is to use the results to produce plant strains that can better serve a growing population in a warming world.

stories.title: Minors living alone on Ceuta's streets at risk of abuse
stories.summary: Several thousand unaccompanied minors have gathered in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on the northern coast of Africa. Illness and abuse are rife, and the authorities admit they are overwhelmed.

stories.title: In drought-stricken France, tankers supply drinking water
stories.summary: France is seeing water shortages in regions that usually have plenty of supply. This summer's extreme heat is exposing how unprepared much of the country, and Europe, is for increasing water scarcity.

stories.title: Who really owns the Caspian Sea?
stories.summary: Five countries border the Caspian Sea, but none owns a fixed share. A 2018 convention established rules for navigation, security and fishing while leaving some seabed borders unresolved.

stories.title: South Korea and Japan stress stress 'critical' US alliance as Trump slashes military drills
stories.summary: Trump made the surprise announcement about the troop drawdown in a social media post just before US and South Korean soldiers began Monday's annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises.

stories.title: UAE says Iran targeted its territory with two missiles after first alert in months
stories.summary: Tuesday's alert was the first in months after a false alarm in June and a July alert for an attack that ultimately did not enter UAE territory. Before that, the last missile warning came in early May.

stories.title: Champagne harvest starts early in France as heatwave speeds ripening
stories.summary: Aerial and close-up footage shows an early Champagne grape harvest in Tours-sur-Marne as heatwaves force smaller crews and faster picking schedules

stories.title: Italian town carries towering Virgin Mary structure through streets
stories.summary: Thousands gather in Sora, Italy, as devotees carry a 16-metre-high illuminated structure through the streets for the Feast of the Assumption.

stories.title: Families' agonising search for answers as thousands still missing in Gaza
stories.summary: Ten months after a ceasefire was declared, thousands of Palestinians in Gaza are still reported missing.

stories.title: Large fire breaks out at recycling centre in southeast London
stories.summary: A large fire breaks out at a recycling centre in Deptford, southeast London, as 15 fire engines and around 100 firefighters tackle the blaze.

stories.title: Australia mushroom killer Erin Patterson's lawyers point to jury irregularities at appeal
stories.summary: Patterson was found guilty last year of murdering her husband's parents and an elderly aunt in 2023 by serving them a beef Wellington lunch laced with lethal death cap mushrooms.

stories.title: Mud baths and red water: inside Bulgaria's Lake Atanasovsko
stories.summary: Tourists slather mud and float in red brine at Lake Atanasovsko, while Pomorie’s salt museum preserves Bulgaria’s fading salt-making heritage.

stories.title: Indonesian authorities seize 2.6 tonnes of meth in major bust, narcotics official says
stories.summary: Indonesia has some of the world's toughest anti-drug laws, including the death penalty for traffickers, but has maintained a moratorium on executions for several years.

stories.title: First jellyfish museum in the US opens in Pompano Beach
stories.summary: Pompano Beach hosts the first US jellyfish museum, where visitors watch 20 species drift in tanks and learn about their ecosystems and research.

stories.title: Fire in building housing several hotels in eastern India kills at least nine, injures six
stories.summary: Some of the victims are believed to be Bangladeshi nationals who had travelled to Kolkata for medical treatment, according to a member of West Bengal’s ruling party.

stories.title: Russians pull billions from banks fearing Kremlin will seize savings for war
stories.summary: Russia's central bank reported that billions of roubles have been withdrawn from banks each month, as Russians pull out cash amid fears of the Kremlin seizing their savings to fund the war in Ukraine amid a deteriorating economy.

stories.title: 'Catastrophic' hotel mix-up at the heart of Australia's mushroom murder appeal
stories.summary: Lawyers for Erin Patterson say her conviction was undermined by a "catastrophic" mix-up that led to the jury staying at the same hotel as prosecutors and a key witness.

stories.title: Iran executed at least 900 people since January, rights group says
stories.summary: The Abdorrahman Boroumand Center documented 901 executions in the first seven months of 2026, including 56 on political or national security charges and 98 members of ethnic minorities — a further rise in death penalties in the Islamic Republic in recent years.

stories.title: Opening statements begin in long-awaited trial almost 30 years after hip-hop star Tupac Shakur was murdered
stories.summary: Duane Davis is being accused of planning the fatal 1996 Las Vegas shooting which claimed the life of hip-hop’s rising star Tupac Shakur. Davis was the first to be charged in connection with the murder, after he was indicted in 2023.
